input: Set up a micro-investing account with spare change

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether they want a fully automated round-up system, a manual recurring deposit, or both determines which platforms and setup steps are relevant.
Whether this is for themselves alone, a partner, or a child (custodial account) changes the account type and legal requirements entirely.
Their country of residence determines which platforms are legally available to them (e.g., Acorns is US-only, Moneybox is UK-only).
Whether they have a hard monthly cap on how much spare change gets invested affects platform choice and configuration of round-up limits.
Their risk tolerance and investment style (e.g., conservative bonds vs. aggressive stocks, ESG focus) determines which portfolio to select inside the platform.
Knowing their end financial goal (emergency fund, long-term wealth, specific purchase) shapes the account type chosen — taxable brokerage, Roth IRA, ISA, etc.
Which bank account or card they plan to link for round-ups determines compatibility with platforms and how quickly they can complete setup.

gold.taskTitle: Set Up a Spare-Change Micro-Investing Account
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to open and configure a micro-investing account that automatically invests spare change from everyday purchases or savings.

questions.title: Should round-ups be automatic or manually triggered?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the user wants a fully hands-off round-up system tied to purchases, a scheduled manual deposit, or a combination of both.

questions.title: Is this account for you, a partner, or a child?
questions.description: Determines if a standard individual account, joint account, or custodial/junior account is needed, which changes platform options and paperwork.

questions.title: Which country are you investing from?
questions.description: Identifies the user's country of residence to filter only the platforms that are legally available and regulated there.

questions.title: Is there a monthly maximum you want to invest?
questions.description: Establishes any hard cap on spare-change contributions per month, which influences platform selection and round-up settings.

questions.title: How would you describe your risk comfort level?
questions.description: Captures the user's risk tolerance and any investment preferences (e.g., ESG, bonds-heavy, growth stocks) to guide portfolio selection within the chosen platform.

questions.title: What is the main financial goal for this account?
questions.description: Determines whether the account is for long-term retirement savings, a mid-term goal, or a general wealth buffer — this dictates the most suitable account type (taxable, Roth IRA, ISA, etc.).

questions.title: Which bank or card will you link for round-ups?
questions.description: Identifies the user's primary spending account or card to verify compatibility with shortlisted micro-investing platforms before committing to one.
